agent_notes: STEPBible lemmatizes sadai under the form shaday (H7704); it is the poetic form of the word for 'field' (sadeh), as all five English versions read it. I glossed it 'the field'.

The verb yishkon is singular after a collective 'of (STEPBible: 'it dwells'); I glossed it as singular and let the translations pluralize. 'Aleihem is read as 'beside them', i.e. the springs and wadis of verses 10-11 (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David).

מעליותיו: STEPBible gives 'from upper rooms'. I keep 'from his upper rooms' (aliyyah, roof-chamber, as in v.3 'who beams his upper rooms in the waters'), reading the clouds as the divine upper storey. Ibn Ezra, Radak, Metzudat David all identify them with clouds. KJV and ASV 'chambers' is acceptable; BBE 'store-houses' is an interpretation.
תשבע: literally 'is sated', the same verb used of eating. KJV 'satisfied' is fair; ASV 'filled' and BBE 'full' lose the appetite image. Kept 'is sated' in the literal layer.

history.note: [consider] Drop 'above the clouds' or say 'from his high rooms in the clouds'. (PS.104.13, Metzudat David: 'מעליותיו. הם העננים'; Radak: 'מעליותיו והם העננים')

agent_notes: לעבודת האדם: STEPBible 'labor of humankind'. KJV 'service of man' is archaic but literal; the Hebrew is the same root as ʿebed, 'servant'. Radak's gloss (plants that need human tilling, as opposed to grass that grows unaided) is cited, but the verse itself does not say so; Metzudat David's reading (dyes and crafts) is a different tradition.

משמן: min with shemen is ambiguous. 'From oil' (so the literal layer) could mean 'shining from oil' (so YLT), or 'more than oil', or 'by means of oil'. Radak and Meiri discuss this. The dramatic layer takes the common reading, faces shining with oil.

Ibn Ezra's comment that bread and wine are mentioned together is brief and I do not cite it for any claim beyond that. Malbim's reading (wine and oil bring joy only together with bread) is his own and I do not follow it in the translation.

ישבעו עצי יהוה: 'trees of YHWH' is read by Radak and Meiri as trees that grow without human planting (superlative, or 'forest trees'); Rashi on Genesis Rabbah says 'in the Garden of Eden'. I follow the first and mention the superlative option. Whether אשר נטע refers to YHWH planting them (most likely) rather than to ordinary planting is clear in the Hebrew.

אשר־שם: STEPBible 'where'. Hebrew has the relative particle and the adverb 'there' together: 'in which there'. KJV 'Where' is correct for sense, but the double marking is lost; literal layer keeps 'which there'.

חסידה: the stork (white stork, Ciconia ciconia) is the standard identification (BDB, HALOT); the name means 'the faithful/loyal one', which many commentators link to its devotion to its young, but Radak and Meiri do not make that point in the packet and I leave sources empty for it. Targum reads וָוְתָא (a different bird name) for the stork; not discussed in the text. ברושים: cypress/juniper (Cupressus sempervirens or Juniperus), not 'fir' as in KJV; this is the standard correction (BDB, HALOT).

history.note: [consider] Say that storks pass through the land in great numbers on their spring and autumn migrations (Jer 8:7), and cite Radak and Meiri for their nesting in tall trees. (PS.104.17, Radak: 'דרכו לקנן בעץ גבוה ומנהגו לקנן בארזים'; Meiri: 'שדרכה לחזור לקנן בברושים')

agent_notes: שפנים: the hyrax (Procavia capensis), the rock hyrax; KJV and ASV 'conies' (an old word for rabbits) is a mistranslation, and BBE 'small beasts' avoids the problem. Hyraxes are not rodents or rabbits; Lev 11:5 lists them with the unclean animals that chew the cud. יעלים: Nubian ibex (Capra nubiana), not 'wild goats'. Meiri cites Job 39:1 (yaʿale-sela, 'ibexes of the rock') for their love of high places.

history.note: [consider] Say that En-gedi had a place called 'the Rocks of the Wild Goats' (1 Sam 24:2). (PS.104.18: לַיְּעֵלִים; 1 Sam 24:3 (Heb.) 'צוּרֵי הַיְּעֵלִים')

agent_notes: מבואו: lit. 'its entrance, its coming in', for the sun it is the setting (Hebrew 'the sun enters'). KJV 'going down' and ASV match; YLT 'place of entrance' is closer to the Hebrew. Radak gives two readings (the sun knows its own coming, or the sun knows the moon's coming) and says the word covers both rising and setting; Rashi takes it to contrast the sun's regularity with the moon's irregular course. Note also that STEPBible glosses 'setting'; I keep 'its entering'.

history.note: [consider] Either drop the complaint about 'curtain' or say only that the English word no longer brings a tent to mind. (PS.104.2: כַּיְרִיעָה, KJV 'like a curtain'; Metzudat Zion: 'כיריעה. כוילון')

agent_notes: חיתו־יער: the final vav on חיתו is the archaic construct ending, flagged by Radak ('the vav is added, like the vav of בנו בעור'). Ibn Ezra says the vav is simply added. Not a pronoun. ירמש (rāmaś) is the verb of Gen 1 for creeping things; KJV 'creep forth' is fine, BBE 'come quietly out of their secret places' adds a motive the Hebrew lacks.
מאל: 'from God' using El, not YHWH. STEPBible links it to deity.yhwh; here El is the generic word for God and the entity link is a harmless approximation. Mentioned for the reviewer.

יאספון, ירבצון: both carry the paragogic nun (-ûn) on the imperfect, a poetic form, and the first is a niphal ('they are gathered/withdraw'). KJV 'they gather themselves together' is acceptable; ASV 'they get them away' is closer to the withdrawal sense, YLT 'they are gathered' is literal. I read 'they withdraw' in the dramatic layer as consistent with Rashi's and Radak's explanation (they hide from people).

history.note: [consider] Use 'they are gathered [in]' in translation_literal and the token gloss, and keep 'withdraw' for the dramatic layer. (PS.104.22: יֵאָסֵפוּן (YLT 'they are gathered'))

agent_notes: פעלו and עבדתו: two near-synonyms for work. KJV 'work ... labour' is fine. Ibn Ezra's one-line comment ('on the contrary, at night he sleeps') is cryptic; I do not rely on it for any claim.

קנינך: STEPBible 'creature[s]'. The word (qinyan) means acquisitions, property, possessions (KJV 'riches', YLT 'possessions'); Rashi connects it with 'creator (qoneh) of heaven and earth' in Gen 14:19. BBE 'the things you have made' is a paraphrase. Radak and Metzudat David read it as 'your possessions'. I gloss it 'your possessions' and flag the 'creature' sense as an alternative via the same root, as in Prov 8:22 (qanani).

The suffix on בּוֹ is ambiguous: 'in it' (the sea) or 'with him' (Leviathan). STEPBible, KJV, ASV and YLT take 'in it'; BBE takes 'a plaything'. I kept 'in it' in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer carry both senses lightly. Rashi on Psalms 104:26 reads it as God playing with Leviathan (citing b. Avodah Zarah 3b and Job 40:29); Radak and Metzudat David read Leviathan as the player.

history.note: [consider] Attribute the God-plays reading to Rashi alone, and cite Meiri and Radak for 'in it', the sea. (PS.104.26, Meiri: 'לשחק בתוך הים לעשות בכל כחפצת נפשו'; Radak: 'לשחק בו פי' בים')
[consider] Smooth the grammar, e.g. 'All of them look to you, waiting for you to give them their food in its season.' (PS.104.27: כֻּלָּם אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּן לָתֵת אָכְלָם בְּעִתּוֹ)

agent_notes: Reviewer request addressed: the commentary now credits the 'as asaf' (gather) reading of tosef to Radak, Meiri and Metzudat Zion, and says that Rashi takes it as 'ending, being finished', citing Ps 73:19 (safu tammu). Ibn Ezra and Metzudat David are not named in the attribution: Ibn Ezra glosses it with a different formulation, and Metzudat David only uses 'gathered' in his paraphrase.

tosef is read from asaf 'gather' (STEPBible lemma H0622), as in the lemma. The KJV and ASV 'takest away' and the BBE 'take away' follow that sense loosely. A reading from yasaf 'add' (as in the Hebrew form itself) would give 'you add their breath', which makes no sense here; hence the commentators' equation with te'esof. Rashi's alternative derivation is from the root of 'end'. I chose 'gather in' for the literal layer and kept the other reading in the note.

STEPBible glosses yibahelun as 'they are terrified'; I kept 'they are dismayed' in the literal layer to keep the sense of sudden panic without overstating terror. The five English versions split between 'troubled' (KJV, ASV, Webster, YLT) and BBE's conditional sentence; I kept the Hebrew's paratactic structure.

history.note: [should_fix] In directors_commentary, credit the 'as asaf' reading to Radak, Meiri and the Metzudot only, and say that Rashi takes tosef as 'ending, being finished' (Ps 73:19), as the note already does. (PS.104.29, Rashi: 'תּוֹסֵף רוּחָם. לְשׁוֹן כִּלָּיוֹן, כְּמוֹ סָפוּ תַמּוּ (תהלים עג:יט)'; Radak: 'תוסף. כמו תאסוף'; Metzudat Zion: 'תוסף. כמו תאסף')

agent_notes: Addressed the reviewer request: 'his upper rooms' is now the direct object of the participle 'the one who beams' (qara, a denominative verb from qorah 'beam'), and the '[of]' is gone. The Hebrew order (beams / in the waters / his upper rooms) is kept, so the object follows the prepositional phrase.

STEPBible glosses hamqareh as 'makes beams for'. I kept the sense 'lays the beams' but glossed it 'the one who beams' to keep the denominative visible. Qara in this sense occurs only here and in Neh 3:3, 6 (qeru, 'they beamed'), which Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion cite.

The commentators split on what the 'upper rooms' are: Ibn Ezra says the clouds, Metzudat David and Malbim the upper waters above the firmament, Meiri the earth as a dwelling. I follow the water-above-the-sky reading as the most natural for 'in the waters', and mention the cloud reading in the commentary. Ugaritic parallels (Baal as rider of the clouds) are my own knowledge and carry no source.

history.note: [should_fix] Rewrite the first clause of translation_literal so that 'his upper rooms' is the object of the verb, e.g. 'The one who beams his upper rooms in the waters', and drop the '[of]'. (PS.104.3: הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו (KJV 'Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters'; YLT 'laying the beam of His upper chambers in the waters'; Metzudat David 'עשה תקרת עליותיו במים'))

agent_notes: רוּחֲךָ is 'your breath/wind/spirit'. The Targum and Rashi (resurrection of the dead) read it as a divine spirit that raises the dead; Radak gives both that and the generational-renewal reading. I translated 'your spirit' in the literal layer and kept 'breath' for v.29 where the same noun is the creature's. The word is the same in both verses, which the commentary points out.

history.note: [consider] Say that the Targum reads 'your holy spirit', and credit the resurrection reading to Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David. (PS.104.30, Targum: 'תְּשַׁלַח רוּחַ קוּדְשָׁךְ מִתְבַּרְיָן'; Rashi: 'בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים'; Metzudat David: 'בזמן התחי׳')

agent_notes: Both verbs are jussive (יְהִי, יִשְׂמַח): a wish, not a prediction. The KJV 'shall endure / shall rejoice' flattens this; ASV and BBE keep 'let'.

Radak's quoted text in the packet continues with a dangling 'ואמר'; I did not rely on it. The Meiri 'Gog and Magog' reading and the Malbim naturalistic reading (earthquake and volcano) are both left out of the commentary; I follow the plain Sinai-theophany reading Rashi cites (Exodus 19:18).
The packet's Radak entry for this verse is headed 'יתמו' and belongs to v.35; I did not cite it here.

history.note: [consider] Say that the KJV's 'my meditation of him' attaches 'him' to the meditation, while the Hebrew attaches it to the verb: 'may my meditation be sweet to him'. (PS.104.34: יֶעֱרַב עָלָיו שִׂיחִי; Metzudat David: 'יומתק עליו תפלתי לקבלה ברצון')

agent_notes: הַלְלוּ־יָהּ is the first 'hallelujah' of Book IV's closing sequence and the last words of the psalm. I rendered it 'Praise Yah' in the literal layer so that the short form of the divine name stays visible. STEPBible's gloss of אֵינָם as 'not they' is kept as 'they are not'. The reading of חַטָּאִים as 'sinners' (people) rather than 'sins' is the standard one; Berakhot 10a, cited by Rashi, famously argues for 'sins' (חֲטָאִים), which is a rabbinic reading I mention in the commentary but do not follow.

The Hebrew can be read 'makes winds his messengers' (ASV, YLT, BBE) or 'makes his messengers winds' (KJV, following Hebrews 1:7 via the Greek). Both objects are unmarked, so word order does not decide. I kept the literal layer neutral in order ('making his messengers winds') and chose the first reading in the dramatic layer, since the surrounding verses are all weather. The commentary says so.

history.note: [consider] Correct the root of bal to בלה, or leave it empty, and render va'ed as 'and perpetuity' or 'for ever and ever'. (PS.104.5: בַּל־תִּמּוֹט עוֹלָם וָעֶד)

agent_notes: The suffix on kisito 'you covered it' refers back to the earth of verse 5 (Radak, Meiri read it so). STEPBible glosses it 'it'; I kept that. Tehom is taken as the covering, with the preposition of means ('with the deep') understood, as Radak notes.

'They went up mountains, they went down valleys' has two readings: the waters flow over mountains and down into valleys (KJV, Radak, Metzudat David), or the mountains rose and the valleys sank (ASV, BBE). The verbs are plural imperfects; harim and beqa'ot are grammatically the subjects or the places. I kept the Hebrew ambiguity in the literal layer and followed the first reading in the dramatic layer.

В синодальном переводе этот псалом — 103-й (греко-славянская нумерация); ссылки на стихи в комментариях даны по еврейскому счёту, как в английском тексте. «Нефеш» передано как «душа моя» в тексте и объяснено в примечании: гортань, дыхание, живое существо со своими нуждами.
«Ломают жажду свою»: буквальный слой сохраняет глагол «ломать», драматический говорит «сламывают» вместо синодального «утоляют», чтобы не потерять образ.
Ma'aliyyotav передано как «горние покои» в буквальном слое («с горних покоев Его») и «с высоких покоев» в драматическом; Синодальный перевод: «с высот Своих».

history.note: [consider] Use one capitalisation for divine pronouns across the chapter's literal layers. (PS.104.13: מֵעֲלִיּוֹתָיו; PS.104.3 literal «верхние покои свои»)

agent_notes: Синодальный перевод читает «ели» (как KJV «fir trees») и «аисту»; в комментарии отмечено, что beroshim — кипарисы или можжевельники. Игра слов хасида/хесед передана пояснением в заметке.

history.note: [consider] Make the pos 7 gloss «дом его», or keep the Hebrew feminine in both places and add a note. (PS.104.17: חֲסִידָה בְּרוֹשִׁים בֵּיתָהּ)

agent_notes: Синодальный перевод: «серны» (ya'el — горный козёл, ибекс) и «зайцы» (shafan — даман, не заяц). В буквальном слое: «горные козлы» и «даманы»; в драматическом — «горным козлам» и «даману».

history.note: [consider] Cite «1 Цар 24:3», or say which numbering is used. (1 Sam 24:3 (Heb.): צוּרֵי הַיְּעֵלִים)

agent_notes: По замечанию рецензента в буквальном слое «Львята рыкающие» заменено на «Молодые львы рыкающие», как в глоссе, примечании и комментарии (кефирим — львы в силе, не львята). Остальные слои оставлены без изменений.

history.note: [should_fix] In translation_literal replace «Львята рыкающие» with «Молодые львы рыкающие», to match the gloss, the note and the commentary. (PS.104.21: הַכְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִים לַטָּרֶף (English literal 'The young lions [are] roaring'; Synodal 'львы ревут'; Radak: young lions in their young manhood))

agent_notes: В буквальном слое yeasefun передано «они уходят, собираются»: страдательный оттенок («их забирают») сохранён в комментарии, а не в тексте.

history.note: [consider] Use one spelling of Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David throughout the chapter, the one used in earlier psalms. (PS.104.3, PS.104.15, PS.104.25 commentaries and notes)

agent_notes: Левиафан: в Синодальном переводе «этот левиафан», «играть с ним». Суффикс в «лесахек бо» двусмыслен (в нём — в море, или с ним — с Левиафаном); в буквальном слое оставлено «в нём», в драматическом выбрано «играть в нём», как в английском слое, а второе прочтение вынесено в комментарий.

«тосэф»: в буквальном слое «Ты собираешь» их дух (чтение от асаф, как у Радака и Меири), а не Синодальное «Ты отнимаешь»; Раши читает иначе («кончается»). Комментарий сохраняет оба чтения. Слово «руах» везде передано «дух» в буквальном слое и «дыхание» в драматическом, как в английских слоях (breath).

Глагол hamqareh («кроющий балками») в буквальном слое передан описательно: «тот, кто кроет балками верхние покои свои над водами»; синодальное «устраиваешь горние чертоги» сохраняет образ высоты, но теряет балки и глагол от существительного, о чём сказано в комментарии.
«Ты посылаешь дух Твой — они созидаются»: Синодальный перевод тоже «созидаются»; «лицо земли» оставлено как в Синодальном, при этом в комментарии объяснено слово «адама» (почва).

«Аллилуйя»: в Синодальном «Аллилуия»; в слоях дано «Хвалите Йаһ» (буквальный) и «Хвалите Господа» (драматический), чтобы сохранить мысль комментария о кратком имени Йаһ. «Йаһ» написано так, как в буквальном слое пишут YHWH, — без перевода.

Порядок «ангелов-духов»: в драматическом слое выбрано прочтение «ветры — вестники», как в английском тексте; синодальное «Ты творишь ангелами Своими духов» следует греческому прочтению (Евр 1:7), это отмечено в комментарии.

Неоднозначность подлежащего сохранена в буквальном слое («поднялись горы, спустились долины»), а в драматическом слое подлежащим выбраны воды, как в английском тексте. Синодальный перевод тоже читает подлежащим воды.
